name: Form layouts
summary: Layouts for whole forms: two columns, sectioned settings, a single inline row and the submit row, plus a helper that warns before leaving with unsaved edits.
description:
.v-form is a size container, so the layouts respond to the space the form has (a sidebar, a card, a dialog), not to the window. Two columns start at 36rem of form width and settings sections sit beside their fields from 48rem.

Add data-v-unsaved to a form to have the browser ask before the page is left with edits.

classes.name: v-form
classes.description: Stacks fields with an even gap and is the size container for the layouts inside.

classes.name: v-form-grid
classes.description: Two columns from 36rem of form width, one below.

classes.name: v-form-full
classes.description: On a field in a .v-form-grid: spans both columns.

classes.name: v-form-section
classes.description: A settings row: title and description beside the fields from 48rem, above them below.

classes.name: v-form-section-header
classes.description: Holds the section title and text.

classes.name: v-form-section-body
classes.description: The section's fields. Also a container, so a grid inside follows the column width.

classes.name: v-form-inline
classes.description: Fields and buttons on one wrapping row, aligned on the control line.

classes.name: v-form-actions
classes.description: The submit row, buttons at the end.

classes.name: v-form-actions-start
classes.description: A note or secondary action pushed to the start of the actions row.

hooks.name: data-v-unsaved
hooks.description: Marks the form dirty on any edit, and the browser asks before the page is left. A submit that goes ahead, or a reset, marks it clean.

events.name: v:dirty
events.description: Fires when the form changes between clean and dirty, from data-v-unsaved.

a11y: Keep the visual order and the source order the same, so Tab moves through the fields as they appear.
Section titles are real headings (h3 or h4), so screen reader users can jump between sections of a long settings page.
An inline form still needs a visible label on every field.
The leave-page warning is the browser's own dialog, so it is accessible and cannot be styled.
